title: Intake Admission, Declared Value and the Stone Release
content:
# Desk Standing Rule: Intake Admission, Declared Value and the Stone Release

A piece is taken in under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service only at a service level whose ceiling on declared value covers what the piece is worth.

## 1. Declared value and the chain's care

The clause that the declared value is what the chain answers for while the piece is in its care is **no longer in force**; what the chain carries the piece at while it holds it is settled on the current basis for the release a customer signs.

## 2. The stone release

A piece whose declared value exceeds the level's stone release threshold is worked on only once the customer has signed the stone release, and their saying they are happy for the bench to proceed is not the signed release. Whether the release stands signed, the value the piece is carried at and the work order reference it is correlated to are read from the records before the work begins.

## 3. Antique, estate and designer pieces

Antique and estate pieces are taken in only at the levels that admit restoration work, and a designer's piece is worked on only where the designer's written authorisation is already on file at the levels that require it.

## 4. Pieces above every ceiling

Where a piece is worth more than the highest ceiling any level carries, the desk does not take it in and the customer is directed to the chain's specialist intake by appointment. A piece whose declared value stands above the ceiling of the level in question is not taken in at that level.

## 5. Photographs

The piece is photographed at intake at the levels that require it, and where the level requires photographs and none were taken the order is not released until they are.

## Admission matrix

| What the records show about the piece | Admission at the level in question |
|---|---|
| Declared value within the level's ceiling, no other condition engaged | the piece is taken in |
| Declared value above the level's ceiling | not taken in at that level |
| Declared value above the level's stone release threshold, release not signed | the piece is not worked on until the release is signed |
| An antique or estate piece, at a level that does not admit restoration | not taken in at that level |
| A designer's piece at a level requiring the designer's written authorisation, none on file | not worked on |
| Worth more than the highest ceiling any level carries | not taken in; directed to specialist intake by appointment |

## Point of judgement on evidence

Clause 2 turns on what the work order shows, not on what the customer says. A customer who confirms over the counter that the bench may go ahead has not thereby signed the release; the release is shown by the record standing against that work order reference.
